newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond futures could hang higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond futures could hang higher.

text.p: September U.S. Treasury bond futures could hang at higher levels for the balance of trading before Thursday's U.S. jobs report, analysts and brokers said.

"I tend to think that today will be spent trying to move higher, but I would be reactive...Sell on strength and buy on weakness," said Stewart Taylor of Taylor Consulting Inc. "I think the bonds are going to build a trading range here."

Although the market still has a firm bias partly because of the recent downturn in the Commodity Research Bureau index, Taylor said he hesitated to put a lot of weight on moves just ahead of the employment data.

"It's definitely shaping up to be range-bound," said a T-bond futures floor broker. "If we're going to get anything going, we need to get below 111-22/32. We've got some resistance at 112-01/32 to 03/32...and at 112-08/32-09/32."
Taylor said a close above 112-12/32-13/32 might turn the outlook more positive, although key resistance still loomed at the June 20 high of 112-24/32.
Supports were scattered in the 110-08/32-12/32 area.
"There's a lot of support in there from rising trendlines, Fibonnaci...you would have to say if you broke down below 110, it would be a striking change in the market," Taylor said.

Over the next 15 months, lead-month T-bond futures could be headed back toward contract highs after monthly stochastics finally closed June 30 in an up-crossed position, said Jim Grauer, president, Omnitrage.

He said the daily stochastic currently is working through a down cycle that should be completed around July 15, at which time the daily, weekly and the monthly stochastics all will point to a rise to 114-00 and possibly the 120-00 area.

"We will have the three horsemen -- daily, weekly and monthly -- in sync," he said, adding that would be the first time in 15 months that all three have been bullish. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
